subject: Burst capacity + snapback sizing for Black Friday pilot
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@acme.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Need sizing help for Black Friday 'snapback' surge

Hi Logan,

We talked briefly on the call this morning — thanks for taking it. We're scoping a dedicated capacity pilot ahead of Black Friday. The tricky part: our traffic tends to plateau and then 'snap back' to a big burst when we release campaign emails. That burst lasts ~10-15 minutes but drives very high concurrency.

Can you send a short questionnaire or template we can fill with telemetry? I'm attaching a small export (prelim_telemetry_export.csv) so you can see the format. High level asks:
- What metrics do you need to recommend a dedicated fleet size for snapback scenarios?
- Is there a quick rule of thumb for burst-to-sustained ratios you use?
- How do you size for p99 latency given bursty arrival patterns?

Goals: PoC by mid-November, final sizing + proposal by end of November.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform
Acme AI

(attachment: prelim_telemetry_export.csv)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Need sizing help for Black Friday 'snapback' surge

Elena — great context, thanks and thanks for the export. I've put together a compact template that will let us produce a recommended fleet sketch and a PoC checklist. Attached: redwood_burst_sizing_template.csv. Can you fill the sections below (short answers are fine) and send the completed CSV back? I also pasted the fields we need inline to speed things up.

Required telemetry / fields (minimum viable):
1) Token mix: median prompt tokens, median response tokens, 75/90/99 token percentiles for responses
2) Request arrival: sample of per-minute requests for the largest 3 burst days (CSV or time-series)
3) Peak concurrency observed (connections / in-flight requests) and typical sustained concurrency
4) Session shape: % of requests that are multi-message sessions, average session length (messages)
5) Expected p50/p90/p99 latency SLOs for the pilot
6) Desired fallback behavior for capacity limits (downgrade to smaller model, queue, 503)
7) Expected PoC traffic schedule (dates/times, expected peak window length)
8) Any regulatory or VPC constraints for Private/Dedicated deployment

Sizing notes / quick guidance:
- For burst windows <20 minutes, we size a short-burst pool scaled to the 95th percentile of burst concurrency with a 1.5x safety factor and a fallback pool for queued tokens.
- Snapback recovery matters: if KV-cache reuse is important (multi-turn), factor in session affinity — otherwise assume cold-start token cost.
- For p99-sensitive workloads, prefer low-oversubscription (<=1.2x) and reserve a small dedicated hot pool to avoid large queuing spikes.

PoC milestones (suggested):
- Day 0-3: ingest telemetry + complete template
- Day 4-7: PoC build (reserved pool + stress harness)
- Day 8-10: Controlled stress run with injected campaign-like traffic
- Day 11: Results review and final proposal

I also asked Karthik to include GPU SKU and quantization guidance — cc'd him. If you can attach the time-series (per-minute) CSV for your top burst day, we can run a quick simulation and share a preliminary fleet sketch.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood_burst_sizing_template.csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Need sizing help for Black Friday 'snapback' surge

Quick technical addendum from my side:

Elena — a couple of practical points to speed the PoC and keep cost reasonable:
- If response medians are <256 tokens, N10-class GPUs with static quantization will likely be cost-optimal for the sustained pool; use an N20-style instance for the hot burst pool if you need lower latency p99.
- Try to provide token-percentile histograms rather than only averages — 90/95/99 are useful for tail sizing.
- If you expect many short multi-turn sessions with high KV-cache reuse, prioritize session pinning to reduce repetitive compute. That changes the sizing math quite a bit (KV-hit reduces token compute).
- For snapback: consider a short-lived overprovisioned buffer (5–10% of expected burst concurrency) that we drain in the first 2 minutes; this reduces queuing and keeps p99 in-check.

I've uploaded a short SKU guide that maps our internal recommendation to commonly available cloud SKUs. Attaching: gpu-sku-recommendation.pdf.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal System Architect | Redwood Inference

(attachment: gpu-sku-recommendation.pdf)

Thanks — pasted answers below (also attached completed CSV and a short telemetry snapshot).

Inline answers:
1) Token mix: median prompt=48, median response=120; response percentiles: p75=160, p90=320, p99=900.
2) Request arrival: attached acme_telemetry_snapshot_20261101.csv (per-minute for Nov 1 campaign test). Peak 1-minute RPS observed: 7,800; sustained baseline ~420 RPS.
3) Peak concurrency observed: 2,300 in-flight during peak minute; typical sustained concurrency ~140.
4) Session shape: ~28% multi-message sessions; avg session length=3.1 messages; KV-cache reuse ~55% for multi-turns.
5) SLOs: pilot p50=70ms, p90=190ms, p99 target<=520ms.
6) Fallback: prefer graceful downgrade to a smaller open model (announce 503 only if queue > 45s).
7) PoC schedule: start Nov 12, controlled run Nov 15 08:00-10:00 PST, final review Nov 18.
8) No special VPC constraints for PoC; production may need VPC.

Next steps: please provide a one-page PoC workback and a rough fleet sketch by Nov 9 so my engineering manager can confirm budgets.

Thanks,
Elena
